finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the unauthenticated query parameter 'q' is interpolated directly into the SQL string via an f-string. An attacker can break out of the LIKE literal and run arbitrary SELECTs, for example a UNION against other tables or columns, to read data from shop.db, such as the owner column or any other table.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: term = request.args.get('q', '') takes the raw user-supplied value with no validation
term is formatted into the SQL text with an f-string, so it is not bound as a parameter
Query results are returned to the caller as JSON, so injected UNION output is exfiltrated directly

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, escaping, or parameter binding on this path. No authentication or authorization decorators on the route. The other two routes (app.py:18, app.py:25) use '?' placeholders, so this route is the outlier. sqlite3 execute() rejects multiple statements, so stacked queries are not possible, but UNION-based and boolean-based extraction still work.

verdict.reason: app.py:11 reads q raw and app.py:12 interpolates it via f-string into db.execute with no auth decorator, validation or binding, and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON, so a 2-column UNION SELECT can exfiltrate data (the parameterized routes at app.py:18 and app.py:25 are not affected).
